justification: Two text changes and no logic: the Ashfield plan name on the controls card now matches the registry and the council's own page (Ashfield DCP 2016, not a hardcoded 2022), and the overdue-check message states the last completed check date instead of a wrong 'twice-monthly' cadence. Nothing is computed differently.

break_it.scenario: The Ashfield label edit accidentally changes the label of another council in the same map.
break_it.what_happens: Another council's controls card would show the wrong plan name beside its controls.
break_it.how: Only the ashfield key's value changed; the other 13 entries are untouched and 292 related tests pass.

break_it.scenario: The plan is overdue but no completed check date is on record (verifiedDateLabel is empty).
break_it.what_happens: The new message would print an empty date or the word undefined.
break_it.how: The text falls back to 'no completed check is on record' when the date label is empty.
break_it.repro: Read the isStale block in ProvisionsByTocStructure.tsx

break_it.scenario: The old Ashfield label is still pinned by a test or a cached page.
break_it.what_happens: A test would fail, or users would see the old name until the cache refreshed.
break_it.how: No test pins the old string (searched tests); the label is read per request by the Python service.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - open an Ashfield address on the live app, Council Rules tab, and confirm the controls card says Inner West Ashfield DCP 2016; Northern Beaches should show the last completed check date in its overdue notice.
